data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed both files and found a standard VCS package: source fetched from the project's own upstream git repository at a pinned tag (#tag=${pkgver}), standard build commands (make all/make install), legitimate dependencies, and SKIP checksums which is normal for VCS sources. The qwen model's inconclusive result was due to API errors (HTTP 400 and LLMResponseError), not security concerns. Notably, qwen's initial PKGBUILD audit (which succeeded) also returned SAFE with identical reasoning about standard VCS practices. No malicious code, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is technical, not substantive. The qwen model experienced API failures (HTTP 400 BadRequestError and LLMResponseError) when attempting to review the files, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model completed successfully and found no issues. There is no actual security disagreement - both models' successful assessments (qwen's initial audit and deepseek's full review) agree the package is safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete file reviews due to API errors (HTTP 400 and LLMResponseError)
learnings: API failures should be distinguished from security findings - a model that crashes or times out should not trigger disagreement escalations when another model successfully completes the review
Initial audits that succeed can provide useful signal even when full file reviews fail due to technical errors
VCS packages with pinned tags and standard build systems are common and safe patterns - models should recognize these quickly without flagging SKIP checksums as concerns
